cells.tense: What you gave up for is finished, and it is still feeding something alive.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Tend one live thing that grew from a cost you paid. Give it the plain care it asks for, and hold the credit loosely while you do.
cells.core:
You can say what a sacrifice cost and stay easy inside the sentence, which most people can't manage — they either shrink it or lean on the person who benefited. The thing you gave up for is still producing, and no ceremony is required for that to be true.

So the care can stay quiet this week. Pick what is alive because of you and give it what it asks for, nothing added. Where the balance wobbles is the moment after: once the good is visible, the pull is to stand near the credit a beat too long. Give the care, then watch yourself. If the thanks shows up, fine. If it doesn't, nothing went wrong with the sacrifice in the first place.
cells.sheetLine: What you gave up is still growing, whether or not anyone says so.
cells.verb: to have what you gave up seen and counted by the people it fed
cells.place: in what you have already become, before the acknowledgment arrives

cells.tense: You are standing in a ceremony that has not been scheduled, waiting to be thanked.
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Find the effort you are keeping up only because someone might see it. Strike that piece and keep the rest of the list going.
cells.core:
A sacrifice is finished and the acknowledgment has not been arranged yet, so the mind builds the parade early: who will notice, when, how it should sound. The future gets run through before anyone has decided anything in the present.

That bracing has a practical cost. When you trade the visible for something quieter, the visible does not announce itself, so the outside keeps not arriving and scanning becomes the work. Find the effort that only survives because it might be seen, and strike it. Then a smaller real thing stands where it can be seen from where you actually are, with no verdict still pending.
cells.sheetLine: You are braced for a thank-you no one has arranged.
cells.verb: to have what you gave up seen and counted by the people it fed
cells.place: in what you have already become, before the acknowledgment arrives

cells.tense: The work is done and holding things up, and you have not stepped into it.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Carry the upkeep of one finished thing on your own reserves, and check nobody's response while it stands.
cells.core:
You make things that last and hold other people up, and the room is different because of them. What is missing is not the evidence — it is the step where you stand inside what you made and take your own measure of it. It sounds like bragging, or like asking for a review that could come back bad, so the step doesn't get taken.

Stand what you made somewhere you can see it. The trying-harder route doesn't reach this; staying with it does. Keep the thing going on what you already have, say nothing about it, and stop scanning for whether anyone registered it. Being enough in your own sight is the whole standard, and it is available now, which is why the ground is so close and so unentered.
cells.sheetLine: What you made works. You have not stood inside it.
cells.verb: to have what you gave up seen and counted by the people it fed
cells.place: in what you have already become, before the acknowledgment arrives

cells.tense: You keep several small things alive, and the account of it comes out as scenery.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Choose the smallest thing only you are keeping alive. Give it steady attention and tell nobody you did. Notice what it draws from you.
cells.core:
You carry what other people chose and keep it working — the household, the health, the last of something hard. That is real caretaking, and it has become the frame of your days. In the telling, though, it comes out as the ordinary backdrop of your life, nothing you would claim.

Start again from the smallest end. One plant, one account, one thing only you are keeping alive — give it steady attention and let nobody hear about it. Then the upkeep can be yours again instead of part of the background. That is the return to the earlier form, where you look after something because it is yours to look after, without needing the world to log the hours.
cells.sheetLine: The upkeep is yours, and the story calls it ordinary.
cells.verb: to have what you gave up seen and counted by the people it fed
cells.place: in what you have already become, before the acknowledgment arrives
